choice: U1 tests with a stalling fake ssh, run on unmodified main: a hanging dashboard push and a hanging device probe both left every cycle gap within interval + 1.5 s
why: the push is a Popen child that is never waited on and each probe runs on its own daemon thread, so neither step blocks the poll thread; the ticket's guess of an uncapped between-cycle step is refuted, so dashboard_push.py and ssh_mux.py stay unchanged

choice: sleep_until ends the between-cycle sleep when either the wall or the monotonic clock reaches poll_seconds, in slices of at most 1 s
why: the sleep is the only step between cycle end and cycle start; time.sleep counts monotonic time, which a box VM pause can stop while the wall clock runs, which fits the 8 min and 4.5 min gaps; this is a guess until the between-cycles line catches a real gap

choice: the sleep also ends on the monotonic deadline
why: a wall clock stepped back (NTP) must not stretch the sleep

choice: a sleep function (PollLoop default and StopAtBoundary default), not a loop inside PollLoop.run
why: StopAtBoundary keeps cycling False for the whole multi-slice sleep, so a SIGTERM there still exits at once

choice: CycleClock.between prints `orch poll: between cycles` only when the gap runs more than SLOW_STEP_SECONDS (10) past poll_seconds, with monotonic seconds and any clock jump
why: names where the time went (ac-1) and tells a VM pause (clock jump) from a blocked thread (no jump) the next time it happens; quiet otherwise

choice: _AfterPoll times backup, dashboard-push and self-deploy through CycleClock.step, names from the fixed AFTER_POLL_STEPS tuple; tracked-read sources and after-poll steps share one per-phase parts map
why: a slow hook inside the cycle shows by name on the cycle end line, the same way tracked-read sources already did

decision: option B (hard caps on after-poll hooks)
why: U1 showed no hook blocks; adding worker threads next to the backup's DB writes adds risk with no observed cause

decision: f-1 slow sleep under a backward clock step
choice: CycleClock.between decides on max(wall, monotonic) elapsed and names a backward step as `clock stepped back`
why: the guard looked at wall time only, so a 45 s monotonic sleep with the wall clock set back 20 s logged nothing; either clock running long now means the gap ran long
